title: "Production Failure Drills"

# Production Failure Drills

This is the lab you keep. One cEOS pair does VLANs, VRRP, and OSPF toward one FRR core. Four hosts sit on two VLANs. You break one piece at a time and write down what still works. That is the production habit. The protocols are the ones this track already built.

## Learning goals

By the end of this chapter you can:

- Draw the failure domain of a trunk, a VRRP master, and an OSPF link before you touch them
- Run three drills and record evidence
- Restore the lab to the starting state
- Say which failures this image set still cannot show

## Shape

```text
        r-frr
        /   \
     sw1     sw2      VRRP .254 on VLAN 10 and VLAN 20
      | \   / |
      |  \ /  |
     h1  h2  h3 h4    h1,h3 VLAN 10 · h2,h4 VLAN 20
```

sw1 and sw2 are cEOS. r-frr is FRR. Hosts are Alpine. Two cEOS plus one FRR fits the host. There is no SR Linux in this lab so the failure notes stay about one design.

| VLAN | Subnet | Gateway | Master |
|------|--------|---------|--------|
| 10 | 172.16.10.0/24 | 172.16.10.254 | sw1 priority 110 |
| 20 | 172.16.20.0/24 | 172.16.20.254 | sw2 priority 110 |

OSPF area 0 on sw1 Ethernet3 — r-frr eth1 (`10.1.1.0/30`) and sw2 Ethernet3 — r-frr eth2 (`10.1.2.0/30`). Each switch advertises its VLAN prefixes. The trunk between sw1 Ethernet4 and sw2 Ethernet4 carries VLAN 10 and 20 so VRRP hellos have a path.

Build it from the VLAN, VRRP, and OSPF chapters. Do not add a fourth heavy node.

Hosts:

| Host | Address | Default |
|------|---------|---------|
| h1, on sw1 | 172.16.10.11/24 | 172.16.10.254 |
| h3, on sw2 | 172.16.10.12/24 | 172.16.10.254 |
| h2, on sw1 | 172.16.20.11/24 | 172.16.20.254 |
| h4, on sw2 | 172.16.20.12/24 | 172.16.20.254 |

## Baseline, before any drill

```bash
docker exec clab-drill-sw1 Cli -c "show vrrp brief"
docker exec clab-drill-r-frr vtysh -c "show ip ospf neighbor"
docker exec clab-drill-h1 ping -c 2 172.16.10.12
docker exec clab-drill-h1 ping -c 2 172.16.20.11
docker exec clab-drill-h1 ping -c 2 10.0.0.1
```

Give r-frr a loopback `10.0.0.1/32` in OSPF so the third ping has a target that is not on the campus VLANs.

All three pings work. sw1 is master for VLAN 10. sw2 is master for VLAN 20. Two OSPF neighbours are Full.

## Drill 1 — trunk VLAN missing

On sw2, remove VLAN 20 from the trunk allowed list.

- h2 stops reaching h4.
- h1 still reaches h3.
- VRRP for VLAN 20 may go dual-master because hellos died. Write down `show vrrp` on both switches.
- Put VLAN 20 back. Masters return to one each. Do not start drill 2 until they have.

## Drill 2 — VRRP master down

Shut Vlan10 on sw1.

- sw2 becomes master for VLAN 10.
- h1 still pings 172.16.10.254 and h3.
- OSPF on sw1 may drop if you shut the whole box instead of the SVI. Shut only Vlan10 so the underlay stays. That is the point: first-hop failure and core adjacency are different layers.
- No shut Vlan10. sw1 preempts.

## Drill 3 — one OSPF uplink

Shut r-frr eth1.

- The neighbour to sw1 goes down. The neighbour to sw2 stays Full.
- h1 still pings h2. Campus traffic does not need r-frr.
- h1's ping to 10.0.0.1 fails if sw1 was the only way and sw1 has no other route. If sw1 still has VLAN OSPF to sw2, the ping may take the long path. Record which one you built. A passive VLAN interface, as in the open-image campus lab, makes the ping fail. An active VLAN OSPF adjacency hides the failure. Choose passive on the SVIs so this drill means something.

## Restore

Unshut every interface. Allowed VLAN list is 10 and 20 on both ends. VRRP masters match the table. Two OSPF neighbours are Full. Then:

```bash
containerlab destroy -t topology.clab.yml --cleanup
```

## What these images still will not show

A wireless client roam, a phone registration, an SD-WAN policy on a controller, and a carrier MPLS VPN are not in this image set. Do not fake them with a static route and call it the same thing. The drills above are the production set this host can prove: broadcast domain, first hop, and IGP, broken one at a time, with the show command written down.
